testName: Air Brakes Test #2 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: For a single vehicle with air brakes, the leakage rate should not exceed ____ in one minute during a static leakage test.
questions.explanation: During a static leakage test on a single vehicle with air brakes, the leakage rate must not exceed 2 psi in one minute. If air leaks faster than this, the vehicle needs repairs and should not be driven.

questions.question: What does an air compressor governor control?

options.text: When the air compressor pumps air into the air storage tanks.
How fast air is pumped into the air storage tanks.
The temperature of the air pumped into the air storage tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the air compressor pumps air into the air storage tanks.
questions.explanation: The air compressor governor controls when the air compressor pumps air into the air storage tanks.

questions.question: What does an application pressure gauge show?

options.text: How much air pressure is being applied to the brakes.
How much air pressure is available.
How much air pressure is needed to stop a vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: How much air pressure is being applied to the brakes.
questions.explanation: An application pressure gauge shows how much air pressure is being applied to the brakes. This helps a driver notice if brakes are starting to fade.

questions.question: What can happen if you do not drain air tanks?

options.text: Water can freeze and cause brake failure.
Too much air collects in the tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Water can freeze and cause brake failure.
questions.explanation: Air tanks must be drained regularly to remove water and compressor oil. If water is not removed, it can freeze in cold weather and cause brake failure.

questions.question: In cold weather, how often should you check your vehicle's alcohol evaporator?
questions.explanation: An alcohol evaporator prevents ice from building up in an air brake system. In cold weather, check and refill the evaporator every day.

questions.question: Where are foundation brakes used?
questions.explanation: Foundation brakes are used on all wheels of a vehicle. The most common type is the s-cam drum brake.

questions.question: What is a benefit of using an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS)?

options.text: It is required in some states.
It gives the driver better control.

questions.correctAnswerText: It gives the driver better control.
questions.explanation: An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) helps provide better control during hard braking, but does not necessarily reduce stopping distance.

questions.question: A slack adjuster should move no more than ____ from where it connects to the push rod.
questions.explanation: Before each trip, pull each slack adjuster to check it. It should not move more than about one inch from where the push rod is attached. If it moves more than one inch, the brakes need adjustment.

questions.question: What can happen if air pressure gets too low in an air brake system?
questions.explanation: Pressing and releasing the brake pedal unnecessarily lets air out of the system faster than the compressor can replace it. If pressure gets too low, the brakes may stop working.

questions.question: Brakes can get out of adjustment quickly, especially when:
questions.explanation: Hot brakes are especially prone to getting out of adjustment. Check your brakes regularly. Properly adjusted brakes on all wheels are essential for safe vehicle control.

questions.question: What should air tank drains be used for?

options.text: Only use them when it rains.

questions.explanation: Air tank drains remove water and oil from the air tanks. Always drain the tanks completely when you use the drain.

questions.question: What does it mean if the safety relief valve releases air from the brake system?

options.text: The air pressure is too high.

questions.correctAnswerText: The air pressure is too high.
questions.explanation: The safety relief valve releases air if the pressure gets too high. If this happens, something is wrong and a mechanic should check the system.

questions.question: What should happen before air pressure drops below 55 psi?

options.text: The warning light should turn on.
The vehicle cannot shift out of gear.

questions.correctAnswerText: The warning light should turn on.
questions.explanation: The low air pressure warning light must turn on before the air pressure drops below 55 psi. If the warning light does not work during an inspection, the vehicle is not safe to drive.

questions.question: What does the air compressor governor do at 125 psi?

options.text: Stop pumping air into the tanks.
Start pumping air into the tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop pumping air into the tanks.
questions.explanation: When the air tanks reach 125 psi, the governor stops the compressor from pumping. This pressure level is called the "cut-out" level.

questions.question: What color light shows that anti-lock brakes are not working?
questions.explanation: Vehicles with Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS) have yellow warning lights that show brake system problems.

questions.question: What does it mean if the safety relief valve releases air?

options.text: Something is wrong with the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Something is wrong with the brakes.
questions.explanation: When the safety relief valve releases air, the brake system has a problem. A mechanic should check it right away.

questions.question: What color are ABS malfunction warning lights?
questions.explanation: ABS malfunction lights are yellow. Even if ABS is not working, your regular brakes will still work.

questions.question: What type of brakes do most new heavy-duty trucks use?
questions.explanation: Most new heavy-duty trucks use dual air brakes. This system has two separate brake systems that use one set of brake controls.

questions.question: What should you never do when spring brakes are on?
questions.explanation: Never push the brake pedal when spring brakes are on. The combined force could damage the brakes.

questions.question: What is the purpose of air storage tanks?

options.text: They are not allowed on vehicles.
They hold compressed air for the brakes.
They should be drained of extra air after every trip.

questions.correctAnswerText: They hold compressed air for the brakes.
questions.explanation: Air storage tanks hold compressed air for the brake system. Different vehicles have different numbers and sizes of tanks.

questions.question: You are braking on dry pavement at 55 mph. How much distance does brake lag add to your total stopping distance?
questions.explanation: Stopping distance has four parts: perception distance, reaction distance, brake lag distance, and braking distance. At 55 mph on dry pavement, brake lag adds about 32 feet to your total stopping distance.

questions.question: What type of force do emergency brakes use?
questions.explanation: Air brake systems have three parts: service brake, parking brake, and emergency brake. Emergency and parking brakes use mechanical force.

questions.question: Front wheel braking works:
questions.explanation: Front wheel braking works in all road conditions. Front wheels rarely skid, even on ice.

questions.question: What color light shows that a vehicle's ABS is not working?
questions.explanation: Vehicles with Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS) have a yellow light that turns on when the ABS is not working.

questions.question: Before driving a vehicle with a dual air brake system, the driver should:

options.text: Let the vehicle warm up to get fuel to the engine.
Let the air compressor build at least 100 psi pressure in both the primary and secondary systems before driving.
Start driving right after the vehicle starts.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let the air compressor build at least 100 psi pressure in both the primary and secondary systems before driving.
questions.explanation: Before driving a vehicle with a dual air brake system, wait for the air compressor to build at least 100 psi pressure in both the primary and secondary systems. Check the air pressure gauges to monitor the levels.
